content: Nateglinide is prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes in individuals whose condition cannot be controlled by diet and exercise alone. It can be used as a standalone treatment or in combination with other medications. Type 2 diabetes is a condition where the body does not use insulin effectively, leading to an inability to regulate blood sugar levels. Nateglinide belongs to a class of drugs called meglitinides, which work by stimulating the pancreas to release insulin, thereby reducing blood glucose levels. Nateglinide is available in tablet form and is typically taken orally three times a day. It should be taken within 30 minutes before a meal or immediately before eating. If you skip a meal, you must also skip the corresponding dose of nateglinide. Conversely, if you add a meal, you should take an additional dose. Your doctor may adjust your dosage based on your response to the medication. It is essential to monitor your blood glucose levels closely and follow the instructions on your prescription label. Do not take more or less of the medication than prescribed, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. While nateglinide helps control diabetes, it does not cure the condition. Continue taking it even if you feel well. This medication may sometimes be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking nateglinide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially albuterol, allergy or cold medications, aspirin, NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), beta-blockers (e.g., propranolol), corticosteroids (e.g., dexamethasone, prednisone), diuretics, epinephrine, estrogens, thyroid medications, and any medications containing alcohol or sugar. Also, disclose any history of liver or pituitary disease, adrenal insufficiency, diabetic ketoacidosis, neuropathy, or type 1 diabetes. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking nateglinide, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, inform your healthcare provider if you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, or if you experience fever, infection, injury, vomiting, or diarrhea, as these conditions may affect your blood sugar levels. Follow all dietary and exercise recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Reducing calorie intake, losing weight, and exercising can improve diabetes management and enhance the effectiveness of nateglinide. Maintain a healthy diet and be cautious with alcohol consumption, as it can lower blood sugar levels. If you forget to take a dose, consult your doctor for specific instructions. Generally, if you have just started eating, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If you have already finished eating or it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Nateglinide may cause changes in blood sugar levels. Be aware of the symptoms of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), such as shakiness, dizziness, sweating, irritability, mood changes, headache, numbness around the mouth, weakness, pale skin, hunger, or clumsy movements. Severe symptoms, such as confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness, require immediate medical attention. Inform your family and friends about these symptoms so they can assist you in an emergency. Symptoms of high blood sugar (hyperglycemia) include extreme thirst, frequent urination, extreme hunger, weakness, and blurred vision. Untreated hyperglycemia can lead to diabetic ketoacidosis, a life-threatening condition. Seek medical attention immediately if you experience symptoms such as dry mouth, upset stomach, vomiting, shortness of breath, fruity-smelling breath, or decreased consciousness. Common side effects of nateglinide include headache, nasal congestion, runny nose, joint pain, back pain, constipation, cough, and flu-like symptoms. Notify your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Store nateglinide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular monitoring of your blood sugar and HbA1c levels. Your doctor will also instruct you on how to check your blood or urine sugar levels at home. Follow these instructions carefully. Maintain good hygiene, clean wounds promptly, and avoid infections. Always wear a diabetic identification bracelet to ensure proper treatment in emergencies. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
